risks.note: Digitide faces competition from large multinational IT-BPM firms, agile digital-native disruptors and hyperscaler ecosystems, all intensifying pressure on market share and pricing (MD&A, Challenges and Risks).

While AI fuels growth it also accelerates disruption of traditional delivery, necessitating continuous reskilling and workforce evolution; AI-led automation may moderate traditional headcount-driven BPM growth, and outcome-linked pricing forces a rethink of how work is priced as AI reduces manual effort - a structural threat to the ~70% of revenue that is BPM-weighted.
risks.risk: AI-led disruption of traditional service delivery models

risks.note: Global data protection regulations including GDPR and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, alongside emerging AI governance frameworks (EU AI Act, sector-specific AI rules in financial services and healthcare), introduce increasing compliance burdens in cross-border engagements.

Shortages in high-demand areas such as AI engineering, cloud architecture and cybersecurity continue to drive hiring costs and attrition, particularly in North America; AI-ready skills are in limited supply industry-wide.

Inflationary pressure, recession concerns, trade policy changes and evolving visa and immigration regulations may delay client decision cycles or constrain outsourcing budgets; the MD&A also cites Gartner's 'uncertainty pause' in discretionary, project-based technology spending and IMF risks tilted to the downside for 2026-27.

Heightened frequency and sophistication of cyberattacks require continuous investment in security infrastructure, compliance and operational resilience; mitigation cited includes advanced threat detection, AI risk validation, red-team adversarial testing, role-based access control and PII detection.

Structural concentration despite improvement: top 30 customers contributed 58.1% of FY26 revenue, top 20 49.3% and top 10 35.8% (versus 61.2%/52.2%/37.9% in FY25). [Provenance: Corporate Overview concentration disclosure, routed to the profile / capex_expansion / registry bundles - no concentration data was routed into risks_esg.]

BFSI remains the largest vertical at 52% of FY26 revenue, and 62.7% of revenue is domestic with 37.3% international, so a BFSI spending pause or an India demand shock transmits directly. [Provenance: Corporate Overview revenue-mix commentary in the profile / capex_expansion bundles.]
